sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned APP for the State and learned counsel for Opposite Party No.2.
2.
The petitioner seeks bail in anticipation of his arrest in a case registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/494 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that being husband, he has been falsely implicated in the instant case by the informant.
It is also submitted that marriage of the petitioner with Opposite Party No.2 was performed in the year 2015.
But then on account of certain differences, the Opposite Party No.2 left her parental home.
It is also submitted that petitioner stays at his village Kumaripur, P.S. Manihari, Distt. Katihar and looks after his Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.7570 of 2024(3) dt.12-09-2024 ailing old mother.

It is submitted that petitioner is willing to keep the Opposite Party No.2 with honour and dignity at his village at Kumaripur where he resides with his ailing mother but then the Opposite Party No.2 is not interested in restituting her conjugal right with the petitioner at his village at Kumaripur.
It is submitted that Opposite Party No.2 is insisting that the petitioner keeps her at Katihar.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Opposite Party No.2 vehemently rebut the said submission of learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and submits that Opposite Party No.2 is willing to restitute her conjugal rights and she willing to accompany the petitioner to his village Kumaripur where he is residing with his ailing mother.
It is also submitted that Opposite Party No.2 shall also look after her mother-in-law properly.

5. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner at this stage submits that he had also filed Matrimonial Case No.137 of 2022 in the Court of learned Principal Judge, Family Court,
Katihar for restituting his conjugal right under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

It is next submitted that since it has been submitted on behalf of the Opposite Party No.2 that she is willing to accompany the petitioner to her matrimonial home at Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.7570 of 2024(3) dt.12-09-2024 Kumaripur, as such, the petitioner on 18.09.2024 shall go to the parental home of the Opposite Party No.2 for fetching her back to her matrimonial home at Kumaripur.

The learned counsel for the petitioner apprehend that it may be a possibility that Opposite Party No.2 shall not accompany him, thus, submits that in proof that he had gone to the house of Opposite Party for fetching her back to her matrimonial home, he will get his presence in the house of the Opposite Party No.2 videographed.

At this stage, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Opposite Party No.2 submits that the moment the petitioner shall come to the parental house of the Opposite Party No.2, the O.P. No.2, without any objection shall willingly accompany the petitioner on the same day or day after.

6. Put up this case on 20.09.2024 within top five cases.
7.
In the meantime, there shall be no coercive action against the petitioner until the anticipatory bail application is finally adjudicated by this Court.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) sanjeev/-
